messages:
Maria: Quick question — for ephemeral traces created during canary runs (ids prefixed with canary-...), what's the approved retention window? Some teams use 7d, others 24h. If these traces touch customer request IDs should we delete after 24h or keep longer? cc @Alex @Jordan
Alex: Security policy (high level) defaults traces to 30d, but there's an exception for ephemeral/debug traces that are explicitly labeled ephemeral. We have a note in the runbook: <https://docs.redwood.com/security/loging-retention#ephemeral-traces> :point_up:
Jordan: If they contain any customer PII we need legal approval before deletion or we need to keep audit logs. Can you confirm whether the canary traces include full request payloads or just headers/latency metrics?
Maria: Canary traces include full request/response for debugging by default. We do strip tokens but there are customer_request_id fields.
Sam: For the last canary we ran (canary-20260315-42) we redacted request bodies with a script before storing. That was a manual step tho. I can share the script.
Sam: Script snippet: `python tools/redact_traces.py --input s3://redwood-traces/canary-20260315-42 --output s3://redwood-traces/redacted/canary-20260315-42`
oncall-sre: If we need to do an immediate one-off purge we can run an S3 delete, but please open a ticket and include customer IDs so we have an audit trail. One-off delete command (example):
```
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-traces --recursive --exclude "*" --include "canary-20260315-42/*"
```
sec-bot: Policy excerpt: "Ephemeral traces may be set to 24h retention when stored with `ephemeral=true` tag and after redaction of PII. Any traces containing identifiable customer data require privacy-team review." (policy ref: SEC-LOG-004)
Alex: TL;DR: If you can guarantee PII is redacted, we can approve 24h TTL for ephemeral canary traces. If not, follow default 30d and loop in privacy/legal for deletion. Security can give the final amber/green on redaction adequacy.
Jordan: @Maria please confirm that the redact script removes `customer_id` and `user.email`. If yes, security can sign off and we can automate TTL.
Maria: Confirmed — redact script replaces `customer_id` and `user.email` with "REDACTED". I'll attach the checksum of the run and open a Jira: INFRA-4572 to request automated 24h TTL for canary bucket and note the redaction step.
Sam: I'll add a small PR to infra-config: `ephemeral_trace_ttl_hours: 24` behind a feature flag so we can flip if needed.
Maria: Cool. For the current canary run I'll request a one-off purge after the redaction job completes. @oncall-sre can you hold off until I post the Jira/Ticket link? :eyes:
oncall-sre: Yup, hold until ticket exists. Post the ticket and ping me and I'll run the deletion. :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks all. Small follow-up: can we add an automated verification step that asserts no `customer_id` fields remain before TTL reduction? If someone can hack that into the redact job, security will be comfortable with the 24h policy.
Sam: I'll add a check that scans a sample of N traces for `customer_id` and fail the job if found. Will link PR in INFRA-4572.
Maria: Filing INFRA-4572 now and will @mention security + privacy. Thanks everyone.
Jordan: Thanks — and please include the redaction script location and the sample verification details in the ticket.
